queries: SELECT SEX, avg_aCL_IgG, avg_ANA, avg_ANA / AVG(avg_ANA) OVER () AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_averages FROM (SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_aCL_IgG, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ANA FROM Examination e INNER JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) t

WITH s AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT sex, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana * 1.0 / AVG(avg_ana) OVER () AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_avgs FROM s

WITH s AS (SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT SEX, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana / AVG(avg_ana) OVER () AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_averages FROM s

responses.sql: SELECT SEX, avg_aCL_IgG, avg_ANA, avg_ANA / AVG(avg_ANA) OVER () AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_averages FROM (SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_aCL_IgG, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ANA FROM Examination e INNER JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) t

assumptions.assumption: Each sex's average is taken over examination rows (not per patient), so patients with more examinations weigh more; NULLs are ignored by AVG, and the aCL IgG and ANA averages each use only rows where that value is present.

The 'mean of the per-sex ANA averages' is the unweighted mean of the group-level ANA averages over the sex groups returned. If any patients have a NULL or blank SEX, they would form their own group and be included in that mean.

responses.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT sex, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana * 1.0 / AVG(avg_ana) OVER () AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_avgs FROM s

assumptions.assumption: Examinations are inner-joined to Patient, so examinations without a matching patient are excluded. Each AVG ignores NULLs separately, so aCL IgG and ANA are averaged over different row sets if their missing values differ.

The 'mean of the per-sex ANA averages' is the unweighted mean of the per-sex averages. It is not the overall ANA mean across all examinations. Any sex group with a NULL or blank SEX value is treated as its own group, and a group whose ANA values are all missing is left out of that mean.

responses.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT SEX, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana / AVG(avg_ana) OVER () AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_averages FROM s

assumptions.assumption: Examinations are linked to patients by an inner join on ID, so examinations with no matching patient are dropped. Averages ignore NULLs. Patients with a NULL or empty SEX form their own group, if any exist.

The 'mean of the per-sex ANA averages' is the unweighted mean of the group-level ANA averages, not the overall ANA average across all examinations. Groups whose ANA average is NULL are excluded from it.
